p_cosa: Serracapriola offers visitors a charming medieval historic centre, rich in architectural and artistic heritage. Walking through the village lanes means immersing yourself in centuries of history, among noble palaces, ancient churches and breathtaking panoramic views over the Fortore plain and the Adriatic.
p_castello: The symbol of Serracapriola. An imposing medieval structure dominating the village. Visitable on request, it offers an exceptional panoramic view over the entire area.
p_sanmercurio: The ancient cathedral dedicated to San Mercurio, patron saint of Serracapriola, is one of the village's religious jewels. The building preserves precious sacred artworks and testifies to centuries of devotion by the local community.
p_padrepio: A place of spirituality and reflection, the convent linked to the figure of Padre Pio is an important religious reference point for the faithful and pilgrims visiting the area.
p_teatropalazzo: The Teatro Palazzo is the cultural heart of Serracapriola. Host to theatre performances, concerts, cultural events and local celebrations, it is a fundamental meeting point for the community and visitors who want to experience the cultural life of the village.
p_palazzo: Historic residence of the feudal family, today partially open to visitors. The building retains original architectural elements that tell the story of noble life in the village.
p_belvedere: A privileged observation point from which to admire the Capitanata landscape, the Fortore plain, Lake Lesina and on clear days even the Croatian coast across the Adriatic.
p_dintorni: The geographic position of Serracapriola makes it an excellent base for exploring some of the most beautiful destinations in northern Puglia and Molise.
p_gargano: One of Italy's most important natural parks. It includes the Foresta Umbra, the Lesina and Varano lagoons, the white cliffs of the promontory and charming villages like Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico. Perfect for hikes, birdwatching and relaxation in nature.
p_lesina: One of Italy's largest coastal lakes, separated from the Adriatic by a thin strip of sand. Famous for its eel, fished by the local population for centuries. The lake hosts numerous waterfowl species and is ideal for nature walks and tasting local products.
p_varano: The largest coastal lake in Puglia, with blue, fish-rich waters. Surrounded by lush vegetation, it offers scenery of great natural beauty. The town of Cagnano Varano on its shores is a picturesque medieval village.
p_lucera: A history-rich city, famous for the majestic Swabian-Angevin Fortress, one of the largest in Europe. It also has a well-preserved Roman amphitheatre, a Gothic cathedral and a characteristic historic centre. Frederick II settled a colony of Saracens here, giving the city a unique history in the Italian context.
p_troia: A small hilltop village with one of the most beautiful Romanesque cathedrals in Puglia, built between the 11th and 12th century. The rose window on the façade is a masterpiece of medieval architecture. The Diocesan Museum holds important sacred artworks.
p_sangiovanni: A world-famous pilgrimage destination where Padre Pio of Pietrelcina lived and worked. The shrine, designed by architect Renzo Piano, is one of the most visited religious sites in the world.
p_montesantangelo: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to the Sanctuary of the Archangel Michael in the grotto where, according to tradition, the Archangel appeared. The historic centre, with its characteristic white houses, is a medieval gem.
p_vieste: The "pearl of the Gargano", with white beaches and crystal-clear waters among the most beautiful in the Mediterranean. The historic centre perched on the promontory is well worth a visit. The famous Sea Caves can be explored by boat.
p_foresta: The green heart of the Gargano Park, the only large beech and deciduous forest in southern Italy. Well-marked trails allow hikes among centuries-old oaks, beeches, holm oaks and maples.
h_termoli: 🏔️ Termoli and the Molise Coast (40 km)
p_termoli: To the north, just a few kilometres away, lies the Molise coast with Termoli, a town with a delightful ancient centre and ferries departing for the Tremiti Islands. The Tremiti are an archipelago of extraordinary natural beauty with clear waters and seabeds teeming with marine life.
p_eno: You cannot visit Serracapriola without tasting the typical local products. The cuisine of the Daunia Apennines is genuine and flavourful, rooted in the peasant and pastoral tradition.
li_eno_1: produced from the centuries-old olive groves of the territory, with an intense and fruity flavour
li_eno_2: robust wines produced from native grape varieties such as Nero di Troia
li_eno_3: Caciocavallo and Pecorino produced with artisan methods
li_eno_4: Cavatelli, orecchiette and tria with traditional sauces
li_eno_5: a typical festive dish, with local aromatic herbs
p_attrazioni: Around Serracapriola there are various leisure attractions suitable for families, children and young people.
p_acquasplash: The Foggia province has seasonal water parks open in the summer months (June–September), with slides, pools, relaxation areas and water games for children and adults. Check opening times and updated prices before visiting.
p_zoo: The largest zoological park in Puglia, near Fasano (BR). It houses hundreds of animal species from around the world: lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras, rhinos and many more. The drive among free-roaming animals is a unique and unforgettable experience, especially for children.
p_lesina_att: Not only a natural wonder but also an ideal place for kayaking, canoeing, sport fishing, birdwatching and cycling and walking paths along the shores. In summer, boat tours are organised to admire the lake and its wildlife.
p_varano_sport: The largest coastal lake in Puglia offers numerous opportunities for water sports and relaxation in nature. Along the shores there are lake bathing facilities and restaurants serving fresh lake fish.
p_parchi: Heading towards Abruzzo, you'll find amusement parks with rides, attractions and shows for families, reachable in about an hour and a half from Serracapriola.
p_riserva: The mouth of the River Fortore, a few kilometres from Serracapriola, is a natural area of great value. Grey herons, storks, flamingos, cormorants and wild ducks populate this wetland. Perfect for photography excursions and sunset walks with views over the Adriatic.
p_equestre: The territory between Serracapriola and the Gargano offers several agritourisms and equestrian centres where you can ride, take horse treks through the countryside and stay in accommodation close to nature.
h_estate: 🎭 Summer in Puglia — festivals and summer events
p_estate: During summer, all of northern Puglia comes alive with music festivals, village fairs, theatre performances and open-air film screenings. Near Serracapriola, events take place in San Severo, Foggia, Lesina and in the villages of the Gargano. Check local calendars to discover the season's events.
